newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Rebellious Tajik commander to withdraw troops.
newsitem.headline: Rebellious Tajik commander to withdraw troops.

text.p: A Tajik commander who had defied his president's orders to pull back to barracks after a clash with an independent armed group, pledged on Thursday to withdraw most of his troops.

"We will be leaving in half an hour," Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev told reporters in the town of Shakhrinau after meeting government negotiators. His troops had clashed with the group on Wednesday near the aluminium-producing town of Tursunzade, about 45 km (30 miles) west of the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
Khudoyberdyev, who heads the Tajik government's elite armoured brigade, said he had moved his troops to Tursunzade to disarm the group, which he accused of stealing weapons from his men last month.
He said there had been a clash on Wednesday morning but that the group's leader, local strongman Kodir Abdulayev, had since fled into nearby hills.

Kudoyberdyev's troops, dozens of heavily armed men, had taken over the local administration building in Tursunzade, about 12 km (8 miles) from Shakhrinau. Five tanks and several armoured vehicles were posted outside.

The commander, who led an armed revolt against the government last year, said he would pull most of them out but leave "a mobile group" to reestablish order. He said he did not think there was any disagreement with President Imamali Rakhmonov, who had ordered him back to base on Wednesday.
